title: Irregular spacing between characters at small font sizes
body: ### Tested versions - Issue does not exist in Godot_v4.4.1-stable_mono_win64 - Issue exists in Godot_v4.5-stable_mono_win64 and Godot_v4.6.1-stable_mono_win64 (Issue introduced between 4.4.1 and 4.5) ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation; 31.0.101.5186) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz (8 threads) - 15.65 GiB memory ### Issue description My game includes pixel art, along with UI rendered at native resolution (using the Canvas Items stretch mode). The window resolution is small (640 x 360), meaning that a normal, non-heading font ends up being relatively small as well (at 8 pixels). With nearest filtering, I've noticed that irregular horizontal spacing can occasionally be seen between text characters in Labels. In v4.4.1, the way I found to remedy this was to set the GUI > Theme > Default Font Subpixel Positioning setting to Disabled. That resulted in a crisp font with regular spacing. However, since Godot v4.5, that change no longer works; the text renders with irregular spacings regardless of what is specified for that setting (or any setting that I can find). Here is an example from 4.4.1, rendering without the irregular spacing: And here is an example from 4.6: Here's a zoomed in comparison to hopefully make it clearer. 4.4.1 is on the top; 4.6 on the bottom. The irregular spacings are underlined in red. Some alternatives I've looked into to try to remedy this issue include: * Using Linear filtering for fonts. This fixes the irregular spacing issues, but makes the text blurry. * Enabling Multichannel Signed Distance Field (MSDF) for the font. The text renders fairly crisply, but text outlines are no longer rendered properly. They all seem to be limited to around 1 pixel or so. A warning explaining this appears on Labels with outlines and the 8 pixel font size: `MSDF font pixel range is too small, some outlines/shadows will not render. Set MSDF pixel range to be at least 32 to render all outlines/shadows.` (32 pixels is way too large for my project, so isn't an option.) Neither of these ends up with parity to the original 4.4.1 text. If nothing changes, I will probably use MSDF, but ideally, I would like it if disabling subpixel positioning for fonts worked like in 4.4.1. That approach combined two things I cannot replicate with current settings: crisp font rendering at small font sizes, along with correct outline rendering. Was this change intentional in order to fix something else? ### Steps to reproduce The MRP includes the following setup steps: 1. Setup a project for pixel art with native resolution UI: * Window Resolution: 640 x 360 * Stretch Mode: Canvas Items * Scale Mode: Integer * Texture Filter: Nearest 2. Under Project Settings GUI > Theme, set Default Font Subpixel Positioning to Disabled. (Advanced settings must be enabled in order to view.) 3. Add a label with a small font size to a scene (8 pixels in this case.) In the MRP, simply run the project to view the sample text. In 4.4.1, the text renders without irregular horizontal spacings between characters. In 4.5 and 4.6, the text has irregular spacings. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [TextBug_4.4.1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25918789/TextBug_4.4.1.zip)
